An estimation of the $B^0_s\rightarrow K^+K^-$ decay time for $B^0_s$ mesons has been made with the help of around 37 picobarns of LHCb data from 2010. This measure allows for constraints on theories beyond the Standard Model that may influence the $B^0_s$ system and is particularly relevant because it is unaffected by uncertainties related to hadron collisions. As a result, it is currently the most accurate standard for $B^0_s$ decay times until more accurate measurements become available with much larger datasets, likely in 2012.

This research paper focuses on the numerical solution of a stochastic control problem governed by a parabolic equation with the control variable affecting the diffusion coefficient, particularly with the presence of rough inputs; it establishes the convergence of a specific numerical discretization method and provides an alternative solution using a stochastic simulation technique known as the Monte-Carlo method.

Our in-depth examination of extremely energetic cosmic rays detected at the Pierre Auger Observatory reveals significant patterns of large-scale anisotropy. At the higher end of our energy spectrum, a specific anisotropy signal was initially reported and our analysis confirms its presence, with an additional finding of an additional anisotropy at intermediate energy levels. A circular anisotropy is apparent in our data sets, with an additional discovery of an octupolar component. We explain our findings through a theoretical framework, suggesting that the anisotropy at the higher end of the energy spectrum may be caused by a large-scale anisotropic distribution of hadronic cosmic ray sources, while an intermediate energy anisotropy could result from energy-dependent morphology of these sources, with morphological features becoming more compact at intermediate energies due to mass injection constraints, and source distributions becoming more anisotropic at higher energies due to mass constraints affecting intermediate energy cosmic rays.

The ATLAS detector at the LHC gathered p+Pb data with a centre of mass energy of 5.02 TeV and 25 nanobarns of integrated luminosity, enabling a comparison with interpolated pp measurements at 2.76 and 7 TeV. Owing to its sophisticated design and reliability, the ATLAS detector successfully collected a comprehensive dataset during heavy ion and proton-proton runs. As a result, it facilitated precise measurements of the nuclear modification factor, obtained by dividing charged particle yields from heavy ion collisions by their proton-proton counterparts in various centrality ranges and rapidity intervals. Furthermore, this analysis reveals a notable variation in the transverse momentum dependence of the nuclear modification factor, with higher $p_T$ values exhibiting greater suppression, particularly in more peripheral collisions.

Quantum mechanics can be explored on noncommutative spaces, characterized by specific commutation relations that define the structure constants of a Lie algebra. By transforming the coordinates into linear differential operators in a commuting momentum space, we can reformulate this issue into an ordinary quantum problem. These operators, representing the coordinates $\hat x_a$, have a form $-i\hat D_a = -iE_{ab}(p)\partial / \partial p_b$, where $E_{ab}$ can be expressed as an infinite series over the deformation parameter $\theta$. The deformed Hamiltonian $\hat H$ describes a symplectic vector whose components derive from $\hat x_a$ and display nontrivial $\theta$-dependent relations related to the Lie algebra. These relations are represented through the structure constants $f_{ab}$ and define a nilpotent algebra when $\hat p$ acts on any state. Consequently, an equivalent description can be given by a set of first-class constraints in classical mechanics and its corresponding counterpart in quantum mechanics, leading to the nilpotency of the algebra. This feature allows us to compute the partition function $Z$ by employing the Weyl algebra and resulting in an expression that depends on the deformation parameter $\theta$. Ultimately, this leads to an analysis of $Z$ in relation to the integer $N$ that represents the number of dimensions, resulting in an identification of the partition function for an $osp(1|2)$ algebra in the ground state

In evaluating the potential of federated learning, we tested its performance in training deep learning models to analyze digitized tissue samples, specifically in a classification application involving the detection of tumor cells within whole-slide images. By simulating a FL environment with a large, diverse dataset of cancer images from various sources, we compared the results of training models using both a federated approach and a centralized approach. Our findings indicate that federated learning can produce models with similar accuracy to those trained with centralized data, while avoiding the need to collect extensive training datasets at a single location. This has significant implications for the development of more reliable image analysis models in histopathology.

In this study, a high-speed optical transmission system is demonstrated, achieving a data rate of 72Gbit/s when using a 50km submarine cable. Chromatic dispersion in the cable is the primary obstacle hindering high-speed data transmission, causing signal distortion. A technique known as pulse shaping can mitigate this effect, but requires precise signal modulation. This paper presents an investigation into the effects of different pulse shaping techniques and their interaction with the phase-sensitive nature of light, leading to the creation of a method for mitigating chromatic dispersion in real-time. The proposed system uses a high-speed pulse shaper based on a microelectromechanical system and a high-speed digital signal processor. Experimental results show that this method can eliminate chromatic dispersion in a 50km submarine cable, significantly improving signal quality.

Deep Learning models like Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCNs) hold great promise for handling time-series data. TCNs leverage a technique called time-dilated convolution that poses an optimization challenge which typically demands significant experimentation. We've developed a technique to automate dilation optimization, enabling efficient search through feasible solutions. Our approach, grounded in the principles of sparse spectral representation, suggests that efficient TCNs can be derived directly from the Discrete Fourier Transform of the input data. Our method simplifies TCN training and eliminates the need for expensive backward propagation. We've demonstrated the effectiveness of our approach by applying it to real-world time-series classification tasks, achieving exceptional performance with up to 75% fewer parameters while maintaining comparable accuracy.
This paper proves that any finite-dimensional Zinbiel algebra over a given field possesses a specific characteristic - nilpotency, building on a previous discovery that these algebras are solvable.

This study provides first-time data on the fluctuations of a specific angle, known as $\Psi_n$, and magnitude, known as $v_n$, related to particle flow, which have been determined using a newly developed technique for four-particle correlations. Researchers used ALICE to collect these data in high-energy Pb-Pb collisions at the LHC. Fluctuations in both angle and magnitude are evident across different centralities and become more pronounced in more central collisions and in collisions where the momentum of the particles is higher than 2 GeV/c. These findings, which have been compared to theoretical models such as iEBE-VISHNU, MUSIC, and AMPT, shed new light on the complex and not well understood initial conditions of these collisions. Furthermore, they highlight unique sensitivities to two crucial factors: the viscosity of quark--gluon plasma and the characteristics of the collisions' initial state. Given that these fluctuations tend to increase with the momentum of the particles, there is a need for re-examining existing theoretical models to gain a more precise and unbiased understanding of quark--gluon plasma's properties.

The unified correspondence theory leverages the algebraic and order theoretic underpinnings of Sahlqvist correspondence to offer versatile tools for correspondence and canonicity across diverse semantic frameworks and signatures. These tools, specifically tailored to logics whose semantics rely on normal lattice expansions (DLEs), enable computation of first-order correspondents for inductive formulas using the algorithm ALBA. Conversely, our proposed method effectively employs ALBA's rules and algebraic language to reverse its computations in the DLE setting, thereby allowing the derivation of an inductive formula from its first-order correspondent.

This research focuses on addressing inconsistencies in data tables that contain missing values and functional relationships. Unlike conventional approaches that require adherence to these dependencies, our work aims to explore theories for handling instances that breach certain dependencies, with no preconditions on the data's completeness. We establish a new framework where some data entries in a table are deemed correct, while others are considered faulty, with no distinction between either group. Furthermore, our framework allows for three types of data encodings, including functional dependencies, existential inequalities, and hypergraphs. A key aspect of our research is examining updating strategies for data sets that incorporate new information and revised requirements. Additionally, we investigate methods for querying our enhanced data sets, as well as identifying inconsistencies within data tables. These advancements contribute to a more comprehensive framework for handling inconsistencies in data sets, which has practical applications in areas like database integration, data cleaning, and database security.

This study presents a novel dynamic econometric model called Time-Varying Poisson AutoRegressive with external covariates, specifically designed to analyze and forecast county-level new daily COVID-19 cases in the United States. Developed using a state-space approach, the TV-PARX model is an advanced model for counting time series, enabling the exploration of changing pandemic dynamics across different regions and time periods. Our methodology is particularly useful for capturing temporary trends and shifts in epidemiological patterns. Our analysis involves estimating the TV-PARX model parameters for 50 U.S. states and forecasts new daily cases from March to December 2020, with results compared to a static Poisson AutoRegressive model. Our findings indicate the TV-PARX model provides more accurate short-term forecasts than the static PARX model, especially during the summer peak period. The TV-PARX model is implemented using the R programming language, and the code is available on GitHub for reproducibility. Our research demonstrates the effectiveness of the TV-PARX model in modeling and forecasting county-level new daily COVID-19 cases.

We introduce Neural Descriptor Fields (NDFs), a novel object representation that
replicates both object points and relative poses in relation to a target, using
category-level descriptors. We apply this representation in object manipulation,
which is typically difficult to model due to grasping's high dimensionality. By
incorporating symmetry, we've created a more manageable space with fewer possible
grasps, and implemented a method to efficiently generate valid grasp poses using
3D convolutional autoencoders. Our system prioritizes poses that it believes the
 Neural Descriptor Fields will accurately describe, which in turn allows for more
precise execution of those grasps, as modeled by a symmetric 3D rotation network.
We've tested NDFs in a simulation environment, and achieved a 73.3% success rate in
grasping and moving objects.

The SiD Detector is one of the two validated detector designs for the future ILC, specifically tailored to meet precision demands for the Higgs boson and other research areas while maintaining an adaptable sensitivity to diverse potential discoveries. The SiD's robust silicon vertex and tracking system, complemented by its high central magnetic field, ensures precise momentum measurement. The detector's finely granulated calorimeter system, designed for particle flow analysis, delivers accurate energy resolution across a wide energy range. Given the approaching construction timeline for the ILC, the time has come to reassess the design choices made during the design phase and incorporate the recent breakthroughs in technology into the review process. This review will discuss R&D prospects and participation opportunities for the SiD's development areas.

We performed a detailed analysis of the properties of four globular clusters located within the Milky Way's satellite galaxy, Fornax, using the VLT/FLAMES survey. Specifically, we investigated the chemical composition of 703 red giant stars within these clusters, including 343 new measurements, and compared our findings to previous results for Ozyman's Tear, Fornax 1, and Tononzintla 2. Our study revealed a diverse range of stars with varying chemical enrichment levels within each cluster. Notably, the Tononzintla 2 cluster exhibited a higher prevalence of nitrogen-enriched stars compared to Ozyman's Tear and Fornax 1. Our analysis also suggested that Tononzintla 2 has a more metal-poor second-generation population with higher [Na/Fe] and [N/Fe] abundance ratios. We found a clear distinction in the [Ba/Fe] abundance among the metal-poor stars with no barium in the most metal-poor group, indicating a possible limitation on cluster's early self-enrichment. A comparison with other Fornax globular clusters showed that Ozyman's Tear and Fornax 1 have a more metal-poor first-generation population with a higher [Ba/Fe] abundance ratio, while Tononzintla 2 and the Dulgi cluster have a more metal-rich second-generation population with lower [Ba/Fe] abundance ratio.

The Isabelle Archive of Formal Proofs has amassed substantial size over recent years, representing a considerable achievement in the realm of formal mathematics. While this accomplishment signifies a major advancement, the ever-expanding nature of the archive presents two primary issues. Firstly, the increased size hinders accessibility to the material, making it harder to navigate and obtain information. Secondly, the growing size diminishes understanding, as it becomes more difficult to grasp the overall architecture and contents. To address these challenges, this paper proposes an automated technique for generating a high-level overview of the archive's directory structure. The proposed method leverages the IsarProofDumper tool to visualize directory structures and incorporates a new command in the Isabelle proof general front-end. Furthermore, this paper showcases the effectiveness of the proposed method by applying it to the Archive of Formal Proofs.

Using the functional renormalization group at the next-to-leading order in the derivative expansion, we have updated the position of the Yang-Lee edge singularity for O(N) universality classes in classic scenarios. Specifically for QCD's relevant universality classes in the 3d Coulomb phase, we have determined $|z_c|/R_\chi^{1/\gamma}$ to be approximately 1.607, 1.589 for $N=2, 4$ respectively. Alternatively, we have also found $|z_c|$ to be around 2.03, 1.83 for $N=2, 4$ in terms of the inverse poincare section width.

In statistics and machine learning, it is frequently essential to establish whether a basic optimization method on a non-convex function can eventually enter a region where the function becomes locally convex. To address this, we developed an inequality that enables us to analyze the properties of the optimization landscape surrounding an approximate solution to a non-convex minimization problem. This inequality is applicable to a broad category of optimization challenges, including problems of this form: Given access to $f(x_0)$ and $f(y_0)$, for functions $f$ and $g$ in specific classes, determine the convexity status of a third function $h$ of interest.

Modern metasurfaces, at the intersection of advanced technology and science,  
constitute an intricate field, involving electromagnetic systems characterized by  
thin, expansive, and minutely featured particles that can also vary spatially,  
temporally, and linearly.  To tackle this intricacy, researchers need to employ a  
unified approach, integrating theoretical design and analysis methods, supported  
by an established framework.  Recent breakthroughs, facilitated by Generalized  
Sheet Transition Conditions in combination with surface susceptibilities,  
now enable designers to develop intricate metasurfaces, addressing longstanding  
challenges.  This paper delves into computational modeling of these complex  
structures through GSCT, discussing how it can resolve longstanding issues and  
facilitate groundbreaking designs.

The primary objective of this research is to validate the smooth local orbital linearization theorem for smooth vector fields with a full set of nearby first integrals, especially those at nondegenerate singular points. This theoretical validation relies heavily on key concepts, including the formal orbital linearization theorem for formally integrable vector fields, the application of the blowing-up technique, and the application of the Sternberg-Chen theorem regarding formally equivalent smooth hyperbolic vector fields.

This report outlines a deep learning approach known as the Electron Correlation
Potential Neural Network (eCPNN), which trains neural networks to approximate various
electron correlation potentials within atomic systems. By learning simplified models
of the electron interaction, eCPNN can efficiently solve many-electron problems.
We present two key neural network architectures: the Direct Method and Implicit
Method. The former directly learns the Hartree-Fock one-body density from input
electron coordinates, while the latter uses an electron correlation potential learned
from electron coordinates, which is applied to a mean-field wavefunction to obtain
the one-body density. Both methods are evaluated on a range of highly challenging
alkali metal and noble gas atoms, demonstrating the Electron Correlation Potential
Neural Network's ability to accurately replicate exact results and achieve significant
speedup over traditional direct configuration interaction methods.

We have serendipitously identified a massive arc-like structure, dubbed a Giant Arc, which lies at a redshift of approximately 0.8. Spanning nearly 1 billion light-years, this feature exhibits remarkable symmetry when viewed from space. It was discovered through a novel approach using intervening magnesium-absorbing systems in the light from background quasars. Our analysis leverages a range of techniques: hierarchical clustering, a statistical test, and power spectrum analysis - each method providing unique insights, which together suggest the presence of a massive structure at around 4.5 to 4.8 sigma confidence levels. We employed multiple statistical tests to mitigate any biases that could influence our findings, which suggest that the arc-like feature is an overdensity with a density ratio of approximately 1.3, with a 30% margin of error. The Giant Arc represents one of the largest and most intriguing examples of a massive cosmic structure that could challenge the cosmological principle underpinning our current understanding of the universe. It may be an early stage in the formation of a massive structure, such as the Sloan Great Wall, which would have emerged around halfway through the universe's age.

While using photometry from stars to monitor the atmosphere may seem straightforward for atmospheric optical depth measurements, especially for variations, a key complication arises with measuring the aerosol vertical optical depth (KV) due to ripples in the measurement errors. This complication is exacerbated by the relatively low sensitivity of photometric measurements to KV. As a result, a significant amount of stellar photometry data is required for an accurate measurement. Despite these challenges, our research has explored various data sets that have yielded promising results. However, our work takes a more rigorous statistical approach that is applicable to more general conditions. We have examined the most effective way to combine different data sets and found that the most precise measurements can be obtained by combining the most accurate results from each data set. Notably, our research has focused on the V band, which is the most commonly used band for KV monitoring. As the most precise measurements for this band have been obtained with the most accurate results from the OGLE-III, OGLE-II and CoRoT data sets, the resulting KV values for these data sets are 0.070, 0.076 and 0.064 respectively. This implies that the most precise measurements for KV have been achieved with an accuracy of 0.064.

Recently, a vast number of techniques have been introduced for estimating a 6D object pose in image data. These methods can be broadly categorized into two main categories based on the supplied information: pose estimation methods provided with 2D-3D correspondences or with 2D object bounding boxes, and those without such information. This research focuses on object pose estimation without specified correspondences or bounding boxes. An issue with existing methods is that they either rely on extensive training datasets or employ time-consuming optimization techniques. In response, we propose a novel pose estimation method, dubbed the Keypoint-Feature Coherence Matrix (KFCM), designed for the challenging scenario without initial clues. The proposed KFCM method directly converts 2D keypoint features into a coherence matrix that represents the spatial distribution of object keypoints. By applying a transformation to the projected 3D object keypoints and calculating the coherence matrix for the resulting keypoints, we can efficiently obtain the target object's pose. Several experiments with a dataset lacking initial clues showed that our proposed method surpasses existing techniques. The code for the Keypoint-Feature Coherence Matrix (KFCM) has been made publicly available on the GitHub repository https://github.com/chenyiyu0447/KFCM.

Peridynamic methods, which utilize integral equations to define bond-based and material-based constitutive laws, offer several advantages including their ability to model fracture and partial damage. The simplest of these, Bond-Based Peridynamics, has the biggest advantage in terms of computational speed due to its straightforward constitutive law. However, both BBPD and MPD face difficulties when modeling materials with non-penetrable interfaces and those that require more complex constitutive laws. Another major limitation of PD is the significant hessian curvature limitation it imposes on the material's deformation. This has led many to believe that PD is only suitable for modeling materials with very soft solid behavior. This research aims to refute this limitation by demonstrating the ability of BBPD to model materials with non-penetrable interfaces and those that require more complex constitutive laws, specifically multiphase materials. This is achieved by introducing an innovative new constitutive law that uses a unique combination of history terms which are able to accurately capture the constitutive behavior of material phase transitions while avoiding the need for auxiliary fields. This new law is applied to a variety of benchmark tests for multiphase materials, including Raveh-Dotan and Benveniste's idealized unit cell test, Taylor impact test, and a 3D plate impact test. The results show that the novel constitutive law can successfully model material phase transitions, while also predicting that the PD solution will converge to the classical FEM solution as the material's memory curve length increases.

We present a new algorithm for sparsely estimating a precision matrix, which originates from a collaborative filtering context and employs a Frobenius-norm penalty. The proposed method, an innovative variant of Graphical Lasso, acquires a distinctive form that facilitates efficient coordinate-wise minimization. Although a direct application of existing Lasso solvers becomes impractical, our method still allows an analytical expression for each block's minimum, enabling the overall problem to be redefined as a set of simpler problems that can be solved coordinately. We establish the convergence proof of our algorithm and provide it as a supplemental material. The innovative algorithm and its theoretical guarantee are the key outcomes of this paper.

Numerous numerical methods for resolving stochastic differential equations in molecular dynamics simulations have been examined and assessed, focusing on differential operators that are solvable, elliptical, and rotation-invariant, as seen in the context of biomolecular dynamics. These studies have investigated the performance of these methods in terms of accuracy, efficiency, and the impact of time-step size on configurational averaging, considering both deterministic and random time steps. The results have shown that the methods differ significantly in terms of accuracy, with some, such as the linearawavedge (LW) scheme, consistently exhibiting greater precision, as demonstrated through the analysis of potential energy and configurational averaging. The LW scheme's superior performance is attributed to its minimal bias in solving the stochastic differential equation, which is a key factor influencing the accuracy of configurational averaging.

Numerical relativity simulations allow us to study how binary black hole mergers interact with their surroundings. However, these simulations start only shortly before the merger and require predetermined initial conditions to proceed. Our research seeks to establish the behavior of dark matter in the moments leading up to a binary black hole merger. We developed a new method to determine whether dark matter becomes distorted or displaced around binary black hole systems of varying mass ratios. Our approach involves comparing the dark matter field to the sum of individual dark matter sub-systems in motion around the binary system. If the dark matter acts as a single, unified entity, its motion can be described through a relative perspective, whereas individual sub-systems moving relative to each other would indicate a multi-component system. We found that for binary systems with significant mass imbalances, dark matter behaves as a single entity with a distinct orientation. Conversely, systems with closer mass ratios cause dark matter to fragment into distinct sub-systems due to oscillating matter waves. Furthermore, when dark matter is in a wave state around binary black hole mergers, its interaction with matter is different from that in static situations.

We tackle the persistent issue of exponential stability for a stretched Euler-Bernoulli beam on a star-shaped graph with three equal branches. The outer points where these branches meet are fixed while rotating. The inner point is capable of moving in two ways, with rotational movement influenced by both elasticity and friction. A mathematical approach transforms this problem into a second-order self-adjoint evolution equation. Then, we use a combination of techniques such as spectral decomposition, operator semigroup theory, and the concept of boundary control to prove the exponential stability of this system. Consequently, this leads to the demonstration of the completeness of eigenvectors associated with pointwise boundary observations. Furthermore, a precise expression for the decay rate of energy is obtained, which demonstrates exponential stability and provides a precise expression for the decay rate.

Researchers utilized acoustic lenses composed of PMMA to increase the detection area of sensitive devices and improve resolution but discovered these lenses introduced image distortion. This problem was investigated and a new lens material called Stycast 1090SI was proposed as an alternative. The acoustic properties of this novel material were examined alongside PMMA to determine its feasibility. Computational simulations and practical tests using two different materials, PMMA and Stycast 1090SI, showed both materials significantly enhance the detection capabilities of sensitive devices. Notably, the Stycast lens exhibited lower levels of distortion compared to the PMMA lens, which could have implications for photoacoustic tomography technology.

Our new method calculates a variation of eigenvector centrality for multi-layered networks that incorporate node importance across different layers. In these networks, defined by separate interconnected graphs without connections between different layers, the value of a node's centrality is determined by the sum of the values of the connected nodes within each specific layer, similar to traditional eigenvector centrality calculations. Unlike standard approaches, our approach takes into account the different network layers these networks exist across, making it ideal for use in citation networks where both paper citations and author collaborations exist simultaneously, with citations representing one layer and author collaborations representing another.

We tackle the issue of non-blind deblurring and demosaicking on noisy raw images using a learning-based approach tailored to handle these images directly, with an innovative new component that simultaneously demosaicks and deblurs them in an interpretable way. To train this model, we utilize real-world camera data transformed into raw images through a realistic process, mimicking real-world camera functions. By doing so, we demonstrate the advantages of our single-stage model over traditional approaches combining demosaicking and deblurring modules, according to objective performance metrics. Additionally, our model's ability to maintain natural image details is showcased through a user study.

Recently, we generated the $R$-Poincar\'e algebra using deformed Poisson brackets, 
which effectively replicate the Fock coordinate transformation. This transformation 
corresponds to a de Sitter spacetime. In this study, we formulate the Dirac equation within 
$R$-Minkowski spacetime and establish that it is analogous to the Dirac equation defined 
within the de Sitter spacetime, described by its conformally flat metric. We then propose 
a novel strategy to solve the Dirac equation within the de Sitter spacetime by adopting 
the Schr\"{o}dinger picture.

This study introduces an open source Python framework that utilizes background knowledge and observational data for the purpose of inferring causal relationships. This framework is comprised of the 'cdt' package, which executes a comprehensive causal discovery process to identify the causal interactions and the causal network structure among the variables, drawing from established methodologies including those from 'Bnlearn' and 'Pcalg', in addition to pairwise algorithms like ANM. The framework is available on GitHub under the terms of the permissive MIT License.

This study investigates how spheres interact with water upon impact, specifically the process known as surface seal that occurs as the sphere enters the water's surface. This surface seal regime, found between low and high-speed impact velocities, features a distinctive "splash dome" formation. Empirical rules describing when the splash dome closes ("pinch-off time") generally hold for both slow-moving and fast-moving spheres, yet require further refinement, especially in the middle speed range. In fact, at mid-range speeds, pinch-off times correlate strongly with the breaking time of a water surface subjected to a similarly mid-range-velocity spherical impact, yet this relationship is not as strong when comparing theoretical and actually observed pinch-off times.

A well-known hypothesis posits that gravity at a quantum level must be devoid of universal symmetries. We investigated an alternative scenario where the $M5$-theory based on a non-compact, spatially bent $M5$-brane possesses a universal symmetry corresponding to a $SU(2)$ algebra. However, our research indicates that this hypothetical scenario is not feasible due to the inability to isolate a relevant low-energy effective field theory containing a $SU(2)$ $\theta$-term within the $M5$-theory's descendants over anti-de Sitter space. Nevertheless, introducing a five-dimensional bulk boundary term leads to the occurrence of generalized $\theta$-terms preserving the $SU(2)$ symmetry in the effective field theories. Consequently, such generalized $\theta$-terms may persist in the context of global symmetries within effective field theories. Additionally, we explored analogous scenarios involving the $D4$-brane system over the anti-de Sitter space, as well as the $M2$-brane theory over the curved seven-dimensional spacetime, with similar outcomes.

Mobile device owners frequently require running sensitive security applications alongside unverified, potentially malicious software, which necessitates reliance on device hardware and system software. 

To enhance trust in devices, specific hardware components can be isolated into separate, securely managed micro-controllers. 

However, integrating multiple hardware domains into a single device complicates security validation. 

This paper introduces an innovative multi-domain hardware design for smartphones, allowing secure execution of critical applications alongside unverified software. 

The design incorporates a unique hardware component that can detect and prevent software-based attacks. 

We showcase the design's effectiveness through the development of several security-critical applications and provide the design's technical specifications, along with a framework for its secure validation. 

This research offers device manufacturers a novel design and set of guidelines for creating secure, multi-domain hardware devices, enabling users to run security-critical applications with confidence.

We investigated the challenges of robust reinforcement learning in scenarios where an adaptive adversary intentionally manipulates rewards and transition probabilities. The adversary's influence is confined to a predetermined fraction $p$ of the total data, and this fraction $p$ is assumed to be a known quantity among which the learner wishes to learn. The learner's primary objective is to devise a policy that can minimize the worst-case cumulative payoffs while withstanding the adversary's attacks, and we established a theoretical limit for optimal performance as $\mathcal{O}(H^{3.5})$, where $H$ represents the episode horizon. We further developed the Natural Policy Gradient (NPG) method and proved that it can achieve an optimal performance of $\mathcal{O}(H^3)$ given sufficient data in the absence of reward corruption, and we demonstrated that a generalization of the NPG method, referred to as the Natural Policy Gradient robust against Adversarial Rewards and Transitions (NPG-ART), is capable of achieving this $\mathcal{O}(H^3)$ optimal performance even in presence of reward corruption. We evaluated the NPG-ART method through a series of experiments using a simple scenario and found that it outperforms multiple robust reinforcement learning baselines.

We uncover an unselectable version of the box game paradox, featuring players making remarkably accurate predictions of unknown real numbers without access to relevant information. Additionally, our analysis confirms the requirement of choice in solving the classic problem and examines alternative configurations of the game.

Our calculations using first-principles methods reveal that cubanite exhibits unusual orbital selectivity, with electrons occupying certain molecular orbitals while being localized in other atomic ones. This phenomenon is exceptionally rare in 3d transition metal compounds, providing a theoretical basis for the experimentally observed lack of charge disproportionation, anomalous Mössbauer spectra, and ferromagnetic coupling between adjacent iron ions.

A new type of photon emission from quantum dots, which emits dark photons due to the involvement of dark excitons, is displaying high on/off ratios and could provide a solution to the problem of blinding in sensors. To fully harness this technology, it's essential to develop a method for controlling the emission of dark photons. Researchers have taken the first step in achieving this by utilizing a nearby photon dot to change the quantum dot's emission properties through the interaction of bright and dark states, an effect they observed in experiments using superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors. This method holds promise for the development of quantum dot-based dark photon systems capable of complex quantum simulations and communication.

Our investigation focuses on a 2D electronic lattice from a non-symmorphic wallpaper group.  We're examining a herringbone-like lattice with two types of glide symmetries using a nearby continuum model. This includes a Dirac cone analysis to determine the topological nature of the lattice near the high-symmetry point along the diagonal of the Brillouin zone. We found that both the lattice and continuum models exhibit similar electronic properties with one insulating and one conducting channel. These results suggest that this lattice has a non-trivial Z2 invariant and a gap can be controlled through an on-site chemical potential. This study is relevant to possible realizations using superlattices of graphene or transition metal dichalcogenides.

Quantum states known as single-photon catalyzed coherent states (SPCCSs) can be generated via quantum-optical catalysis using beam splitters or parametric amplifiers. These states occur when a coherent state and a single-photon state interact in two input ports, and a photon is detected in a specific output channel. We examine the success probabilities associated with detecting these states, as they vary depending on the catalytic device used. Notably, our analysis reveals that states produced by beam splitters and parametric amplifiers exhibit the same characteristics when analyzing the distribution of photons. We thoroughly investigate the unique quantum properties of SPCCSs, including sub-Poisson statistics, anti-bunching effects, and quadrature squeezing. These findings demonstrate that SPCCSs possess abundant non-classical behavior, thereby conferring a quantum advantage for executing various technological tasks.

In General Relativity using the Newman-Penrose formalism, the use of bivectors plays a key role in identifying the precise solutions to Einstein's field equations. This review focuses on explaining the fundamental principles and detailed calculations of bivectors within the Newman-Penrose formalism, specifically by converting a complex self-dual electromagnetic field from the standard Minkowski space basis to the complex null tetrad basis. As a result, we derive the complex coefficients of the Weyl tensor in the context of Newman-Penrose formalism.

A recent framework combining artificial neural networks and mixed integer linear programming for designing chemical compounds has been built upon to create a new method for polymer inference. This new method incorporates a unique way of depicting polymers using monomers, new descriptors that capture their structure, and employs linear regression in the predictive framework. Computational trials have demonstrated that the proposed approach excels in predicting specific chemical properties in polymers, also successfully modeling compounds composed of up to 50 non-hydrogen atoms within a monomeric structure.

This paper examines the application of computational methods for solving certain types of optimal control problems and dynamic games. Issues with state constraints, singular controls, and differential inclusion can be addressed using a combination of techniques, including the use of a support function, a relaxation method, and a dual method. These methods, developed in previous work, can be seen as implementations of the concept of solving a continuous-time dynamic optimization problem by first solving a related discrete-time problem. The paper then discusses the employment of these methods in specific contexts, such as reference tracking problems and the solution of linear stochastic differential games. The effectiveness of these methods is illustrated through concrete examples, with simulated results provided.

Accurate manual delineation of esophageal tumors on CT scans is crucial for radiation therapy planning, yet this process is complicated and error-prone due to several factors, including the soft nature of the esophagus and difficulty in identifying tumor boundaries from the images. In this study, a multi-step segmentation technique is introduced to automate this process. Initially, a coarse delineation is created using a convolutional neural network, which is then refined through a combination of geometric transformations and a UNet network to eliminate any esophageal wall segmentations. The resulting output from this process is compared to that of a single-feed UNet network and a radiologist's manual delineation. Statistics indicating precision, recall, and the Dice coefficient were calculated for both the FRODA dataset and the OASIS dataset after each method was evaluated five times to minimize bias effects. The results showed the proposed technique yielded higher Dice coefficients of 0.793 and 0.819 for the OASIS and FRODA datasets, respectively, as well as better precision and recall statistics, compared to the single-feed UNet network. In particular, the proposed technique demonstrated improved performance on difficult cases, achieving a Dice coefficient of 0.733 for the FRODA dataset, which indicates a significant improvement over the single-feed UNet network with a Dice coefficient of 0.485.

The expense associated with drilling offshore wells is significant, as is the risk of discovering dry wells once drilling is completed. Geosteering, a drilling technique, aims to locate and extract oil or gas while drilling, thanks in part to real-time geophysical observations obtained from downhole sensors. The challenge lies in interpreting the data streams generated in real-time to accurately understand the surrounding formation structure in order to make informed decisions quickly. One crucial aspect in this process is estimating the formation's thickness, which, however, is often accomplished using traditional methods that assume a linear relationship between the interface and the measurement data. However, such methods fail to account for the measurements' uncertainties, which are, however, crucial for making informed decisions under uncertainty. We employ Gaussian process regression, a non-parametric modeling technique that takes into consideration the measurements' uncertainties, to estimate the formation thickness interface. The method is tested using a real-world case study from the Niger Delta and the results indicate that it is possible to use Gaussian process regression to accurately estimate the formation thickness interface and its uncertainty, which can be utilized to create a more precise and realistic model of the target layer.

Named entity recognition (NER) is a fundamental task in natural language processing and a core extraction technique commonly applied to text from the internet. Although conventional NER approaches focus on individual entities, the rising demand for nested entity information requires new methodologies. To address this, we propose a novel holistic structure for modeling nested named entities, incorporating a new type of graph convolutional network designed for filled paths in entity graphs. Our approach not only enhances nested entity typing accuracy but also offers a type-based interpretation for existing zero-shot NER methods, according to the lattice structure of the entity annotations. Our results show significant improvements in state-of-the-art scores for the WiDE benchmark and provide comparative analyses to existing nested NER approaches, achieving 85.0 F1-score without additional training data and 90.2 F1-score with additional training.

We extend the use of tropical methods to counting in arithmetic problems, such as enumerating objects in higher-dimensional spaces using values from specific algebraic structures, over fields that have been modified to have special values. We investigate the enumeration of curves as they intersect other curves, specifically looking at how these intersections change as the underlying field changes. We show that by using a technique called degeneration, we can count these intersections more easily. We find that using this method, the number of intersections that contribute to the count follows a specific mathematical pattern when the underlying field changes. This pattern is related to the number of times a certain geometric shape is repeated when the underlying field changes. We can use this understanding to count these intersections more efficiently. We apply this understanding to count a specific type of curve over fields that have special values, finding that the number of curves grows very quickly as the underlying field changes.

Research into the location detection of mobile nodes within wireless sensor networks is currently ongoing. We propose a novel algorithm for location detection that utilizes a mobile node's connections to adjacent sensor nodes to determine its position. However, this algorithm requires the mobile node to visit multiple locations within the network. We investigate an improved version of the algorithm, which can locate the mobile node more efficiently. The results of our simulations demonstrate that the new algorithm can determine the mobile node's location with fewer visits, and also provide data on the relationship between the number of locations and the number of visits required.

Multilingual individuals possess a high level of proficiency in two or more languages, enabling effective written and oral communication across multiple languages. When communicating, they may blend languages, also known as code-switching or code-mixing, by switching between different languages within a single utterance. This research explores current NLP developments, constraints, and potential obstacles in tackling five critical issues affecting multilingual communities: crisis management, healthcare, election campaigns, fake news dissemination, and hate speech. To move forward, we outline potential future datasets, models, and resources to enhance NLP applications for societal betterment, exemplified through an analysis of code-mixing between English and Hindi but with implications for other language combinations.

Human-generated descriptions are commonly used to train and evaluate image description systems, which are typically ranked based on their similarity to these descriptions. This method's reliability hinges on the quality of these descriptions. Since, as demonstrated in Section 2, current datasets are inadequate, I believe we require more precise guidelines balancing visually impaired users' needs and practical description generation feasibility. High-quality reference data could be ideal for system evaluation, yet we should also consider other alternatives.

Tantalum oxide compounds with the formula Ta$_2$O$_5$ and TaO$_2$N have unique optical and chemical characteristics that make them highly versatile materials with a wide range of potential uses. In a study published recently, the optical properties of Ta$_2$O$_5$ and TaO$_2$N were precisely measured using synchrotron radiation at different temperatures between 300 K and 873 K. The findings from this study were used to create a realistic model of how these materials interact with light, which can be applied to determine the energy lost by hadrons as they pass through the materials. With this information, researchers can better design targets and detect the particles' outputs in hadrontherapy treatments for cancer. The study also highlights the potential for TaO$_2$N to enhance detection efficiency due to its higher radiation density than Ta$_2$O$_5$.

Previous research attributed the spread of misinformation on social media to various factors, including user personality, but a new study suggests this phenomenon occurs on a larger scale, influenced by regional characteristics and demographics. Analyzing Twitter data and additional sources from 2017 to 2020, the researchers examined the circulation of real and false news across 50 US states. They found that certain personality traits, such as conscientiousness and openness, are linked to the dissemination of news, including misinformation, whereas agreeableness and extroversion exhibit no significant correlation. The spread of news and misinformation varies significantly across states, with no clear correlation between them, indicating that local factors play a crucial role. In contrast to urban and rural population demographics, the spread of news and misinformation shows distinct differences, with false news circulating more widely. The researchers also identified key state groups with similar demographic characteristics and news circulation patterns, providing insight into the complex factors contributing to the spread of misinformation.

We introduce a groundbreaking, efficient, and user-friendly detection algorithm called Half-Space Time-Series (HSTS) designed to identify anomalous occurrences in high-frequency data streams. HSTS leverages semi-supervised machine learning and a cutting-edge time-series representation called Prototypes, harnessing minimal expert guidance to achieve precise results. This innovative method first creates a prototype of a normal data dimension using an extremely simple and effective algorithm called Prototype Generation Tree (PGT). The prototype serves as a reference point for a semi-supervised learning technique called Half-Space Method (HSM) to build an optimized detection boundary. The boundary is optimized to minimize false positives while enclosing the vast majority of data points, representing normal events. The key features of HSTS include: (1) extremely efficient construction of prototypes and detection boundaries; (2) extremely low storage requirements; (3) flexible, modular design allowing integration with various data types and detection schemes; and (3) user-friendly implementation. The algorithm's effectiveness is demonstrated through real-world applications, including the detection of energy consumption anomalies and medical data analysis.

Humans employ spoken language to efficiently teach other people new skills. Although robotic demonstrations are a primary teaching method, little research has focused on audio feedback from human instructors. This study investigates the potential of learning from audio input containing both task-related and irrelevant information. Based on data collected during robotic kitchen tasks, three features were extracted from audio recordings of human instructors: semantic content, paralinguistic cues, and acoustic characteristics. A neural network was trained on these features in conjunction with video data of robotic demonstrations, using a combination of multimodal fusion techniques. Results showed that robotic performance improved with both audio and visual input, particularly when relying solely on audio input containing semantic content and irrelevant background noise. Robotic navigation capabilities also improved with acoustic characteristics of the instructor's voice, demonstrating the potential of audio feedback in enhancing robotic skill development through human instruction.

Building on previous work, we propose an algorithm to randomly generate ordered trees of any degree, based on a pre-specified sequence of numbers representing possible node connections. Our method allows for the generation of binary, n-ary trees, or those with various connection patterns. We demonstrate that this algorithm is both accurate and efficient, running in O(n) time with 'n' representing the number of desired nodes. Additionally, we explore potential applications of the algorithm, illustrating its use in deriving formulas by utilizing the underlying proof of correctness.

Quantum field theory complexity is particularly hard to define, especially when transitioning beyond simple free models and their corresponding Gaussian representations. A promising approach to address this difficulty is through the study of conformal field theories in 1+1 dimensions, specifically focusing on the universal sector of the energy-momentum tensor in this context. A key unifying framework consists of Euler-Arnold equations and their broader integro-differential generalizations, ensuring the well-posedness of state or operator complexity optimization problems. Our comprehensive investigation extends upon our prior findings in arXiv:2005.02415, delving into intricate details of employed methodologies. A notable discussion is the examination of differential complexity measures as optimization boundaries, in addition to analyzing the relationship between employed optimization methods and the underlying conformal field theories. Furthermore, our research is supplemented by an illustrative numerical example, showcasing how one-dimensional conformal field theories can be utilized in deriving differential complexity measures.

Conversational interfaces are becoming ubiquitous, and systems with these interfaces are being widely used in various settings by many individuals. Although they have achieved considerable success, the infrastructure for automated testing of these systems lags behind traditional software systems. To enhance the quality of conversational systems, developers require a robust automated testing framework that streamlines the process of crafting, executing, and updating test cases. This paper outlines our ongoing research in developing an automated testing framework for conversational agents in Python, and highlights the key challenges faced in this endeavor. Specifically, we highlight the difficulties in establishing a precise specification for desired system behavior and comparing the meaning of utterances.

Using a sophisticated mathematical model known as the Fisher information matrix, it's possible to estimate the measurement uncertainties $\sigma$ associated with detecting a hypothetical "Planet X" by analyzing its impact on the gravitational field of the known planets. Based on existing measurements from the Juno, Cassini, and Mars-orbiting spacecraft, a  statistical model forecasts a best-case scenario uncertainty of $\sigma=3.3\times 10^{-10}$ AU$^{-1}$ for determining the transverse cross-sectional area of "Planet X" at a distance of 400 AU from the Sun. If we assume "Planet X" has the same mass as the Earth, the predicted median value of $\sigma$ is 0.077 AU$^{2}$, and the 95th percentile is significantly lower at 0.032 AU$^{2}$. It's worth noting that the gravitational effects of "Planet X" would likely be revealed through a non-circularity in the orbits of the detected planets, and a simplified analysis suggests that a possible solution could be verified through a new ground-based telescope survey capable of observing the known planets from 0.2 to 0.8 AU from the Sun.

Previous studies have demonstrated that Translation Memory (TM) can enhance Neural Machine Translation (NMT) performance. Unlike existing approaches which rely on bilingual corpora for TM and employ source-side similarity searches, our proposed framework leverages monolingual data and retrieves memories in a cross-lingual manner. Notably, our framework offers two significant advantages: firstly, it enables vast amounts of monolingual data to be incorporated into TM; secondly, both the memory network and the retrieval process are end-to-end trainable. Experimental results indicate that the proposed method achieves significant performance gains of up to +2.33 BLEU points for each additional translation segment, surpassing the baseline NMT model by over 1.0 BLEU point in 3 out of 3 evaluation sets.

Researchers have suggested that specific patterns in the Cosmic Microwave Background, namely low-variance circles and Hawking points, could provide evidence for the Conformal Cyclic Cosmology model. These patterns are predicted to originate from previous black hole mergers and evaporation events. We analyzed the Planck and WMAP data and found low-variance circles with specific characteristics, which are consistent with the expectations of the Conformal Cyclic Cosmology model. Additionally, our analysis indicates that these patterns are likely the result of a specific type of multipoles. Although the detection is tentative, it aligns with the predictions of the Conformal Cyclic Cosmology model and suggests that the CCc2 network may have a string-like structure. Further investigation is necessary to verify these findings.

This paper builds upon previous work of the second author with Daskalopoulos and Vazquez, which involved introducing a Yamabe flow based on fractional curvature and demonstrating the existence of mild solutions. The current research expands on that study by establishing the convergence of the flow under certain data conditions within a broader framework. The new results are derived from an approach simplified by Struwe in his book.

To recognize new categories from minimal labeled data, few-shot learning has been rapidly evolving in recent years. However, traditional methods that average features over support and query sets often struggle due to the inclusion of noisy information. Furthermore, existing methods primarily focus on selecting representative samples rather than exploiting epistemic uncertainty to exclude confident predictions. In response, we introduce a new probabilistic framework called the Epistemic Uncertainty-based Model (EU-model) to tackle this challenge. EU-model utilizes a novel uncertainty-based contrastive prediction loss to develop a more efficient and effective way of distinguishing new categories from background noise. We evaluate EU-model through a real-world artistic style classification task, where it outperforms state-of-the-art baselines by achieving a 72.1% accuracy rate from just five shots.

Cross-domain recommendation has been gaining significant attention for addressing the challenge of user cold start and overfitting in recommendation systems. By integrating multiple sparse domains, our proposed Multi-Sparse-Domain Collaborative Recommendation (MSDCR) model offers a more realistic and effective solution for enhancing recommendation performance. In contrast to traditional cross-domain recommendation methods, MSDCR harnesses the value of multiple sparse domains through a transfer learning mechanism, directly addressing the sparsity issue in each domain. This allows MSDCR to exploit both domain-specific and cross-domain preferences. Specifically, MSDCR employs multiple domain-specific and a single cross-domain preference matrices in a pairwise collaborative filtering framework. It then incorporates a cross-domain preference enhancement (CPAE) module to capture latent cross-domain interactions and incorporate these insights back into the cross-domain preference matrix. We have experimentally validated MSDCR's efficacy on two real-world datasets, with results indicating that MSDCR outperforms state-of-the-art algorithms, including DeepCrossNetwork and Wide & Deep, in terms of recommendation accuracy. Moreover, MSDCR's scalability and efficiency have been demonstrated through large-scale experimentations.

Convex optimization issues often take on a more manageable form when represented with conic formulations that leverage a wide variety of exotic cones. Exotic cones in this context, refer to specialized geometric shapes with properties enabling efficient implementation of computational tools, specifically barrier oracles for their own and dual shapes. This work introduces Hypatia, an interior-point solver designed to handle these complex shapes with ease. Developed using Julia and interfacing with JuMP, Hypatia can utilize a wide assortment of predefined exotic cones. It then generates simplified equivalent formulations for various optimization applications that can provide significant improvements in processing speed and memory consumption. The proposed method demonstrates a marked improvement in problem-solving efficiency when compared to more conventional and complex conic formulations.

The increasing complexity and quantity of MRI data necessitate automated quality control to ensure reliable analysis. Several methods exist, but a comprehensive evaluation is missing. We conducted a thorough comparison of different techniques for automated quality control in MRI analysis. Initially, 12,799 MRI scans from ORI-DB were used to evaluate the methods' effectiveness. The results showed significant variations depending on the evaluation criteria, field strength, and anatomical region. A scoring system was developed to rank the methods, and the top performers were identified for brain MRI analysis. The top methods demonstrated excellent performance, with mean absolute errors of less than 2 mm in all directions. Our study provides a systematic evaluation of automated quality control methods and offers insights for developing and refining such systems. Additionally, we made available the ranked methods and data for replication and further research on the quality control repository.

To understand how private electric vehicles influence the recovery of power grids following outages, we developed a mathematical framework that incorporates decentralized decision-making in both transportation and energy systems. We utilized multi-agent optimization to model this process and overcame computational challenges through an efficient algorithm based on precise reformation. Numerical analysis was conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, yielding valuable policy insights and paving the way for further study into grid resilience with private EVs within interconnected transportation networks.

Intel's Optane DC Persistent Memory Module, a cutting-edge memory technology, offers fast access similar to DRAM and data persistence similar to SSD, thereby revolutionizing the way applications manage memory.  In this research, we seek to provide system administrators with a tool to manage Optane memory efficiently.  We have developed optanectl, an open-source management platform designed to optimize Optane memory performance.  This system identifies optimal Optane memory allocation strategies, leveraging the unique characteristics of persistent memory to enhance system speed and efficiency.  We have also tested optanectl on various workloads and observed notable speed improvements of up to 10 times and 4 times on Linux and Windows respectively, and a significant performance gain of 60% on a database application.  Moreover, our findings reveal that conventional memory management techniques may lead to performance degradation, whereas optanectl's strategic allocation yields better results at a minimal computational cost.  We believe that our research and optanectl can benefit the growing community of users utilizing Optane memory.

The Motivation Dynamics framework, a concept explored in recent studies that applies bifurcations to model an autonomous agent's decision-making processes, is further developed to accommodate multiple autonomous entities in this paper. We demonstrate how the framework's capabilities can be expanded to capture persistent, cooperative behavior between agents meeting at a specific location, and through in-depth analysis and numerical data, reveal how the new solution's stability arises from a homoclinic rupture bifurcation.

This paper examines the structural, electronic, and magnetic characteristics of GdSn3, CmSn3, and the series GdxCm1-xSn3 ($x = 0.25$, $0.5$, and $0.75$) using a full-potential linearized augmented plane wave method within the generalized gradient approximation+U. We studied the fundamental properties of bulk GdSn3, CmSn3, and GdxCm1-xSn3 materials crystallizing in the AuCu3 structure. Our results match previous experimental and theoretical data on the GdSn3 compound and indicate that CmSn3 and GdSn3 both adopt a type-A anti-ferromagnetic configuration and display metallic behavior. Notably, the magnetic moment diminishes with increasing Cm content in the GdxCm1-xSn3 series, and these materials share some key characteristics, rendering them promising for spintronic technology applications.

The paper reviews predictions made by an extension of the standard model called the bilepton model, which involves changing the fundamental symmetry group from $SU(2) \times U(1)$ to $SU(3) \times U(1)$, while assigning the three fermion families in a non-consecutive manner. For consistency, three fermion families are necessary as indicated by triangle anomaly cancellation and asymptotic freedom. In the bilepton model, novel physical processes are possible due to additional gauge bosons, leading to increased production opportunities for new particles. For instance, a pair of bileptons can be created through processes such as proton-proton collisions resulting in lepton pairs with high invariant masses. Furthermore, a modification to the Higgs mechanism is proposed, which could result in a more massive Higgs boson. Nevertheless, the bilepton model can be experimentally tested and rejected through analysis of high-energy collisions at the Large Hadron Collider.

The concept of ordered generating sequences (OGS) extends a fundamental property of finite abelian groups to non-abelian groups, providing a distinct generalization. According to its definition, any element within a group can be expressed as a product of various generator powers, arranged in a specific order. For the symmetric group Sn, R. Shwartz established a significant link between the ordered generating sequences and the standard Coxeter presentation. Our study extends Shwartz's findings to the finite classical Coxeter group Bn by establishing a similar connection and identifying a symbolic form for each sequence's order, given by a product of generators and powers, which directly correlates with the natural order of the elements in Sn.

Utilizing the Pantheon SN Ia dataset and Sloan Digital Sky Survey, we've developed a method to calculate weak lensing convergence by combining data on galaxy positions and velocities. A correlation between this method and the residual luminosity of Type Ia supernovae reveals a consistent value of $f$, equal to 0.02 with a narrow confidence interval. Accounting for a possible deviation in $f$ from unity, we found that a variation of $f$ from 1 would result in a minimal impact on the Hubble constant $H_0$ estimation. Notably, a variation in $f$ would have a more pronounced effect on $H_0$ when using the combined dataset of SN Ia and Baryon Acoustic Oscillations. Furthermore, we constrained the ratio of matter density to the critical density at $z=0.40$ to be $\Omega_m(0.40) = 0.31 \pm 0.05$ independently of $H_0$.

These are lecture notes for a 6-hour mini-course on stochastic partial differential equations presented at the University of Oxford in April-May 2021. 

The main objective of these lecture notes is to provide an in-depth explanation of the variational method for monotone and coercive stochastic partial differential equations. 

The necessary background on Hilbert space-based functional analysis, operator theory, and stochastic analysis has been recapitulated within the lecture notes and further relevant references are included. 

The concluding chapter covers the pathwise approach.

The development of efficient and controllable quantum communication networks will depend heavily on reliable creation and manipulation of solid-state devices that interface photons with electronic spins effectively. In silicon material, T-type damage centers have shown significant potential for this interface, thanks to their unique optical properties in the O-band region and long-lived electronic spin lifetimes. Although research on these defect centers has so far been conducted as part of bulk silicon studies, we demonstrate the consistent creation of high T center densities within the 220nm device layer of Silicon-On-Insulator (SOI) wafers, using a process that combines ion implantation and heat treatment. By developing a method to measure spin-photon interactions directly, we found that the creation of a single-excition state in these defects requires approximately 1 nanosecond, and that the subsequent transmission of a 10 Gbit/s data stream through these interfaces induces a 0.3 dB attenuation, while maintaining the same spin state. This research represents a significant advancement for quantum communication networks, offering a reliable and efficient method for creating a photon-spin interface, and a feasible way to transfer high-frequency data through these devices.

MRI technology utilizes radio waves to scan the human body and obtain precise, pain-free diagnostic images. These images enable radiologists to visually assess anatomy and physiological processes within the body, ultimately facilitating early disease diagnosis and treatment. Advanced imaging capabilities, combined with sophisticated processing techniques, enable detection of hard-to-spot tumors. This assignment delves into Automated Tumor Detection by comparing conventional image processing methods, such as morphological analysis and regional growth algorithms, in order to explore their application and effectiveness.

In this research, we explore the properties and expressions of a novel algebraic variant of the degenerate Bernoulli polynomial $\tilde{\beta}_{k}(m,x)$, as well as its corresponding degenerate Bernoulli number. This investigation is grounded in a modified algebraic interpretation of the Bernoulli polynomial and number, and is informed by our previous study of the homogenous algebraic variant of the Archimedean zeta function.

The high activity levels of M dwarfs present a significant challenge for discovering exoplanets, as their stellar activity masks the signals from these celestial bodies. This problem requires an effective method for filtering out the stellar activity to reveal the planet's presence. We've developed a novel approach to separating the stellar activity and planetary signals in M dwarfs. First, we identified the most prominent oscillation modes in a set of M dwarfs' Kepler photometry, which account for about 90% of the variability. We then removed these modes from the data and found that the residual shows a random pattern, indicating no detectable oscillation mode in the remaining component. Furthermore, we found that the amplitude of the removed modes is directly proportional to the overall stellar variability, allowing us to remove all modes across a broader frequency range using this proportional relationship. This new technique enhances the detection of planets in M dwarfs, particularly in the Kepler-432 system, where it yields four additional candidate planets and confirms the existence of a low-mass planet.

This research paper proposes a pair of methods for designing a flexible and efficient data collection process in Wireless Sensor Networks, ensuring high reliability and performance. Firstly, a link quality estimation technique is utilized, enabling swift computation of link quality between nodes. Secondly, a hierarchical sector-based system is established to organize and coordinate nodes within each sector to minimize interference and improve data transmission. The effectiveness of these methods was demonstrated through a protocol, HiCC, developed and evaluated in a simulated environment utilizing TinyOS and TelosB devices. The outcome showed that HiCC can achieve very high reliability levels, particularly in large-scale networks and networks prone to bottlenecks.

Deep neural network-based object detectors have achieved high performance in various tasks, but their ability to utilize context also varies greatly. We can categorize object detectors into spatially-agnostic, spatially-contextual, and field-based based on their context usage. Our research aims to enhance context awareness in object detectors through the use of a grid map representation, a common visualization for multi-object information. We contend that grid maps provide a clear context and serve as an effective input for deep neural network-based object detectors. To support this claim, our studies demonstrate the efficient inference and robust recognition capabilities of these detectors when utilizing grid maps. Furthermore, our research includes the ObjectContext (OCXT) dataset, the first publicly available dataset containing 3D objects represented as image contexts, along with the corresponding code and dataset.

The main objective of this paper is to investigate multiple solution possibilities for a specific Kirchhoff type elliptic system of equations that are given by the system of equations where $m\left(\sum_{i=1}^{N}\|u_{i}\|^{2}\right)\Delta u_{i}(x)=|u_{i}(x)|^{p-2}u_{i}(x)$ for $i=1,2,...,N$ and $x\in\omega,\; u_{i}(x)=0$ for $x\in\partial\omega$ where $u_{i}$ and $p$ are given. It's worth noting that when $N=1$, this type of equation is well-researched, particularly regarding the existence of multiple solutions, but such research does not apply to the Kirchhoff type elliptic system of equations. To address this gap, we use variational methods and critical point theory to show that when $p=2$, the system of equations has multiple solutions, provided that certain conditions are met regarding $m,$ $\omega,$ and $N$.

We explore recent developments in the context of random vector spaces, specifically the Rayleigh distribution and its variants. Our study extends the strong Rayleigh property from scalar to matrix-valued contexts, establishing new inequalities and providing specific examples for polynomial spaces and matrix operators. Our findings generalize previous results on the Wishart distribution and lead to new subgaussian and operator bounds. The paper concludes with potential applications and future research directions in the field.

Let $k$ be a perfect field of characteristic greater than two, and consider the ring of power series $R$ over the Witt vectors of $k$, expanded in variables $t_1, \dots, t_d$. The main aim of this study is to generalize classical Fontaine-Messing theory to a base ring of the form $R$. Notably, we establish theorems enabling the comparison of crystalline and \'etale cohomologies with torsion coefficients for smooth schemes $X$ over $R$.

This study explores the double longitudinal-spin asymmetry in semi-inclusive deep inelastic scattering where hadron pairs' transverse momentum is not considered. Specifically, we investigate the cause of the cosine azimuthal asymmetry in hadron production, accounting for the connection between the helicity distribution $g_1$ and the transverse momentum of partons. This analysis applies the sum rules for the double longitudinal-spin asymmetry, taking into account the contributions from quarks and diquarks as represented by the twist-2 and twist-3 distributions, respectively. Furthermore, we examine the role of the diquark's wave function in the case of polarized proton.

We've developed a formal framework for deformed Special Relativity that is based on the Fock transformation, which is a simplified version of the Kirchhoff transformation. This new framework has been applied to a specific scenario where a particle is subject to an external potential, resulting in the derivation of a Schr\"{o}dinger-like equation for both the momentum and position operators. Furthermore, this new framework enables the computation of the Casimir energy, yielding an energy value that is half as large as the predicted value derived from Quantum Electrodynamics.

Wilberd van der Kallen translated this 1951 thesis into English, originally written by T.A. Springer. Springer investigated the method of categorizing conjugacy classes within the symplectic group Sp_n(K), specifically focusing on fields K with a characteristic other than two. His work revealed that each conjugacy class can be distinguished using a combination of invariant characteristics. These characteristics initially mirror those found in the general linear group – namely, irreducible polynomials and systems of non-negative integers – but also incorporate additional properties, such as unique configurations of Hermitian forms and quadratic forms, each belonging to a specific equivalence class.

This paper presents a Wikipedia-based entity recommendation framework that utilizes an embedding approach, where the Wikipedia database is hierarchically divided into layered graphs to extract entity features and learn entity representations. By combining the extracted information with a lightweight ranking method, this framework effectively suggests related entities to users on Wikipedia. We evaluate our approach through both offline and real-world online tests, demonstrating that our embeddings and recommendations exhibit high quality and user engagement. Furthermore, this framework delivers entity recommendations in both English and non-English languages for the Yahoo! Knowledge Graph, where Wikipedia constitutes a fundamental subset.

A key obstacle in kidney transplants arises from the incompatibility between donors and patients, which has been exacerbated by the growing scarcity of kidney donors. Desensitization techniques were developed to overcome these incompatibilities, but they complicate the transplant process, leading to higher risks and costly procedures. Patients who undergo incompatible kidney transplants face higher risks of transplant rejection, dialysis, and secondary complications. Those who successfully transplant kidneys from incompatible donors face a higher risk of graft rejection and a reduced graft lifespan. This paper presents a mathematical model that aims to minimize the expected lifetime treatment costs for patients waiting for kidney transplants, including the option to undergo incompatible transplants. This model is applied to analyze the impact of desensitization techniques, kidney transplants from incompatible donors, dialysis complications, and graft rejection on treatment costs.

Implicit copulas are the primary choice for analyzing complex dependencies due to their ability to effectively model dependence in high-dimensional spaces. The creation of a new generator for a specific implicit copula called the Clayton copula is the focus of this research. The new generator is based on a custom-made multivariate distribution that incorporates a specific implicit copula and a randomly selected vector. The research establishes that this new generator is capable of being inverted, resulting in the derivation of an expression that can be used to generate samples from the Clayton copula. Furthermore, this study demonstrates that the inverse relationship between the copula and its generator can be exploited to develop a new simulation method. This method, known as the inverse generator method, enables the generation of copula-based samples directly from a specified implicit copula.
