to handle out-of-domain data, activation pattern visibility, inclusion of 
subword information, use of a second evaluation network, inclusion of tree 
structure information, and whether scores are directly interpretable. We designed 
a general-purpose scoring framework that incorporates a subword-based BERT 
encoder and a sequential evaluation network, with multiple evaluation networks 
providing additional benefits. Our method includes a subword-based semantic 
interpreter that enhances transparency and a tree-structured module for grammar 
awareness. The code is openly accessible on GitHub at https://github.com/ 
zhengyiyi1993/ASEGS.

The power law decay $p(t,x) \sim t^{-\phi(x,b)/2}$ holds, where $p(t,x)$ is the probability that, during the interval $[1,t]$, the random walk $S$ with zero-mean increments has spent a fraction of time greater than $x$ with non-negative values, occurring for a walk that is defined by finitely many i.i.d. increment values. The parameter $\phi(x,b)$ is determined by the probability $\mathbb{P}(\text{L\'evy}(1/2,\kappa(x,b))<0)$ where $\kappa(x,b) = \frac{\sqrt{1-x}b-\sqrt{1+x}}{\sqrt{1-x}b+\sqrt{1+x}}$ with $b = b_S \geq 0$ indicating the relative magnitude between positive and negative excursions of the random walk.

The ICRF test facility IShTAR at the Max-Planck Institute for Plasma Physics in Germany is designed to investigate how plasma interacts with radio frequency waves. A plasma source with a 0.1 meter length and 0.4 meter diameter provides plasma necessary for the experiment, and features a helical antenna to produce high-density plasma in the helicon mode of discharge. Until now, it was unclear if this plasma source could achieve helicon mode, which is essential for it to function effectively. A study was conducted to verify this capability, involving detailed analysis of plasma parameters and particle power balance using a global model. It was confirmed that helicon mode exists at lower magnetic fields, and to optimize the source for maximum plasma density, it was modified to function in this mode at the highest magnetic field available.

In comparison to conventional chemical pesticides, microbial pesticides exhibit numerous advantages, which can be modelled through a system where entomopathogenic nematodes are used to eliminate and concurrently suppress the population of target insects. This system aims to manage pests through a continuous nematode release mechanism, where the model's equilibrium and Hopf bifurcation periodic solutions are analyzed for optimal pest control, which is further confirmed by numerical simulations and case studies.

While gold-standard pathological diagnosis is highly reliable, it demands a lot of time and resources due to its manual nature.  To accelerate diagnosis, a common solution is to use automatic tumor segmentation methods, based on deep learning, which reduce expert workload and minimize subjectivity.  Nevertheless, developing accurate nucleus segmentation models is a challenging task because of the variability in cell morphology and image quality.  To address this challenge, the current work presents a new approach, where a convolutional neural network is used to generate high-quality nucleus images from whole-cell images, and then the newly acquired images are fed to a nucleus segmentation model.  Experimental results on real cancer diagnosis datasets demonstrate that this two-stage approach can produce accurate nucleus segmentation with limited training data.  Furthermore, the introduced nucleus generation network contributes to a significant enhancement in segmentation precision and a notable reduction in the required training samples.

Let's consider a non-Archimedean local field of characteristic not two and denote it by F. Additionally, let G be either a specific type of special orthogonal group with an odd number of dimensions or a symplectic group with a specific dimensionality, denoted as SO(2r+1)(F) or Sp(2r)(F) respectively. This paper focuses on establishing the local converse theorem for the representation of G. To this end, for two given irreducible admissible generic representations of G, with shared central character and gamma factors, our result stipulates that these representations are isomorphic. To prove this, we draw from the Cogdell, Shahidi, and Tsai framework of partial Bessel functions and the categorization of irreducible generic representations. Furthermore, our result extends the earlier works by Jiang and Soudry as well as Q. Zhang, by expanding on their results for the cases with supercuspidal representations in a wider set of characteristic settings.

Xiong and Liu previously provided a definition for graphs G that have hamiltonian n-th iterated line graphs, L^n(G), where n is 2 or greater. In this study, we examine whether an L^n(G) graph possesses a hamiltonian path, and offer a definition for G to achieve this condition. Additionally, we apply this definition to set multiple upper limits for a graph's hamiltonian path index.

Cell death due to pyroptosis, characterized by inflammation, can contribute to the high cytokine levels seen in severe cases of COVID-19. Pyroptosis is primarily initiated through the NLRP3 inflammasome's formation, which can be triggered by SARS-CoV-2 infection. Research has shown that some anti-inflammatory medications are capable of halting the NLRP3 inflammasome's formation, thereby delaying pyroptotic cell death. Our study aims to investigate the underlying mechanisms governing pyroptosis induced by SARS-CoV-2 infection and to identify potential targets for intervention. Through a combination of computational modeling and analysis of clinical samples and organ culture data, we demonstrate that SARS-CoV-2 infection prompts pyroptotic cell death in the lungs and leads to increased cytokine production in the gastrointestinal system. Furthermore, we found that SARS-CoV-2's ability to induce NLRP3 inflammasome formation and pyroptosis is linked to the severity of respiratory complications. However, treatment with anti-inflammatory medications such as colchicine was shown to delay pyroptotic cell death.

External influences affecting states and reward signals can hinder reinforcement learning by introducing unanticipated fluctuations in the reward signal. This concept is mathematically formalized, and the conditions are identified under which an environment involving uncontrollable state variables can be broken down into two separate components: an environment solely affected by the uncontrollable state and reward variables, and an environment defined by the variables that can be controlled. Furthermore, a condition for reducing the complexity of these variables in Monte Carlo policy evaluation is established, leading to potential acceleration of this process. This acceleration could be applied across a broader range of reinforcement learning algorithms.

A blockchain-based smart contract is an automated transaction program, utilized in various cryptocurrencies, that runs on a decentralized network. Due to the decentralized nature, debugging and analyzing contracts becomes intricate, requiring a different approach than traditional methods. Our innovative approach combines a technique called symbolic execution with a state exploration method to detect and pinpoint the sources of errors within contracts by simulating the program's execution and examining possible paths. This groundbreaking technique enables efficient error localization by generating a minimal test case, in contrast to conventional methods that often result in extensive, hard-to-analyze code. Our groundbreaking method effectively complements existing debugging tools, offering error localization without affecting the underlying contract, in addition to providing actionable insights for contract refinement.

Deep Neural Network structures, specifically Graph Convolutional Neural Networks (GCNNs), have gained popularity in processing complex and irregular data patterns, notably in image analysis applications. We provide an in-depth exploration of GCNNs' fundamental workings, with a focus on the underlying mathematics that governs their behavior. By relating GCNN components to traditional Fourier analysis and applying this understanding to visualize filter mappings, we offer a step-by-step explanation of how GCNNs operate. We use this mathematical framework to derive a new convolution layer formulation, leading to improved network performance as measured by accuracy.

In a three-dimensional spacetime, Einstein's gravity theory is combined with a complex scalar field, and conservative, static, point-source solutions are found, which exhibit scalar soliton behavior. The solutions involve a non-uniform cosmic string and an anti-soliton configuration, both acting as scalar field sources. The research demonstrates that both soliton and anti-soliton solutions can exist, and both display flat spacetime cosmic string behavior. A condition is established that must be met for both soliton and anti-soliton to coexist, and it is proven that the coexistence requires the combination of gravitational and scalar field self-interactions. The research further shows that the soliton and anti-soliton solutions can only exist in pairs when the gravitational and scalar field self-interactions interact in a specific, non-tensorial way.

Theories of supersymmetric Yang-Mills with algebra so(4N) can have non-trivial, invertible-defying symmetries. By utilizing holographic duality, we can determine branes that act as non-trivial, local algebraic expressions for some of these symmetries in specific, adiabatic limits. The branes' forms correspond to specific geometric configurations involving NS-branes, fundamental strings, and D3-branes, and can be classified based on the charge of the corresponding symmetry. Furthermore, our analysis reveals that the entanglement entropy associated with these non-trivial symmetries follows an algebraic form consistent with a random matrix theory.

Elastography, an advancing imaging technique, allows the non-invasive visualisation of tissue pathologies by identifying the physical properties of tissues. Accurate estimation of mechanical properties relies on precise measurement of tissue displacement in multiple directions. Notably, the estimation of shear strain is the most challenging due to limited information available from the correlation of Axial Spatial Autocorrelation function. The availability of additional information from the Virtual Source Synthetic Aperture (VSSA) imaging technique enhances the estimation of shear strain. Compared to traditional Synthetic Aperture (SA) imaging, VSSA provides additional information from the autocorrelation of B-scans in the lateral direction, thereby facilitating the estimation of shear strain. This work introduces a new elastography imaging method, termed Virtual Source Synthetic Aperture (VSSA), and incorporates B-mode data obtained from ultrasound systems to develop the new technique. Simulation and experimental studies were conducted to evaluate the proposed VSSA technique. Simulation results demonstrated that VSSA strain estimates exhibited minimal variance (0.033) in comparison to SA (0.085), 1-D Phantom results showed accurate estimation of shear strain (0.26), while results from soft tissue elasticity testing and ex vivo hard tissue elasticity testing validated the proposed VSSA technique.

Imperative algorithms and logical proofs in sequent calculus or natural deduction coexist as distinct yet related concepts. This interconnection suggests a fundamental equivalence, which we can express as the notion that imperative algorithms essentially embody a form of proofs with cut operations. This equivalence serves as the foundation for an expanded framework, which we call "logical pseudocodes." Each statement in logical pseudocodes is analogous to a step in natural deduction, ensuring correctness and safety in accordance with the original specifications. This approach can be seen as a natural extension to the concept of a computability logic web, but now incorporating the capacity for forward reasoning.

The concept of Boolean Ramsey numbers for sets of posets was initially explored in relation to Boolean lattices and posets obtained from chains with minimal elements combined into a V-shaped structure. A key objective is to establish a minimum number 'n' for any number of color options where a given V-shaped poset will be entirely colored with a specific color in a Boolean lattice. Recent work has led to the determination of Boolean Ramsey numbers for specific instances, and this paper aims to build on that by investigating the same concept for V-shaped posets and identifying minimum posets containing the Ramsey property in Boolean lattices of a particular size. Another area of research within this paper focuses on Boolean rainbow Ramsey numbers which involve identifying either a monochromatic structure or a structure with different color components within a Boolean lattice. This study explores this concept for V-shaped posets and their antichains.

In the context of dynamic data streams, where Euclidean space points are added or removed from a dataset, we develop a one-pass coreset algorithm for solving the $k$-means clustering problem. Our solution employs storage capacity of approximately $k$ times a polynomial function of the dimension $d$ and base-2 logarithm of the number of points $n$, resulting in a total storage capacity of $O(k \cdot d \cdot \log^2 n)$. We build upon the work of [4,5,14] by extending our algorithm to handle updates in the data stream. Furthermore, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our algorithm through experimental evaluations.

We introduce a novel hierarchical strategy for resolving large-scale discrete stochastic pursuit-evasion games on grid worlds by subdividing the environment into'macro-states'. This approach splits decision-making into two separate resolutions: a set of smaller-scale games at the individual state level, and a comprehensive aggregated game representing the overall grid structure. Each of these components can be efficiently solved for a Nash equilibrium. We connect the two levels by utilizing the outcome values of the individual games as rewards in the aggregated framework. Through extensive simulations, our hierarchical model demonstrates substantial computational efficiency improvements while achieving comparable performance to flat Nash policies.

This work builds upon a concept introduced in a 2008 paper by N. Cressie and S. P. Rustagi that categorized a set of n random variables as either cyclic or non-cyclic based on specific characteristics. We here expand this characteristic set to its most general form, making it applicable to any probability distribution or mixture of distributions. Additionally, our revised definition clarifies the distinction between cyclic and non-cyclic n-tuples in a way that is independent of any particular transformation. Our findings also establish the relationship between the original variables and their corresponding transformed variables in the context of exchangeability and the ability to generate a sequence of random variables with specific characteristics.

Recently, deep learning techniques have gained popularity for enhancing low-dose CT images because of their impressive performance and simplicity. A key method in this context is the cycleGAN architecture, which has been successfully applied to improve the quality of low-dose CT images. However, the primary limitation of this approach is the requirement for a large well-processed CT dataset as a reference, which is often difficult to obtain. Furthermore, the cycleGAN training process can be challenging due to the lack of control over the image transformation process. In response to these challenges, we propose a new method, specifically a single-switchable cycleGAN (SS-cGAN) design, which incorporates an adjustable generator that can convert both low-dose CT images and regular-dose CT images. We also designed a novel loss function for the SS-cGAN, which includes a new adversarial loss function, a cycle consistency loss function with a rotation transformation, and a well-processed dose loss function. Our experimental results show that the SS-cGAN can produce more realistic images and accurately maintain the anatomical structure. Moreover, the SS-cGAN requires significantly fewer training parameters compared to the traditional cycleGAN architecture.

Recent successes in dialog understanding tasks can be attributed to pre-training methods with contrastive learning objectives, however current methods solely consider similar dialog samples as positive examples, which may not capture intricate semantic relationships between distant dialog parts. To address this limitation, this study introduces a tree-structured pre-trained conversation model, it first employs a contrastive pre-training method to group related dialog parts and constructs a semantic tree, then employs hierarchical contrastive learning to model the dialog understanding tasks, ultimately leveraging the dialog tree to inform pre-training, reducing noise and potential biases. Experimental results show that the proposed method outperforms baseline models in dialog state tracking and semantic role labeling tasks, while examination of model performance along with case studies help shed light on practical applications and potential limitations of this research.

This research aims to examine the geometric makeup of an ideal fluid's spacetime 
when coupled with a torsion-forming vector field and the relationship between the 
conformal Ricci-Yamabe metric and the conformal eta-Ricci-Yamabe metric. We first 
derive conditions for the conformal Ricci-Yamabe soliton to be in a state of 
expansion, stability, or contraction. Subsequently, we establish a Laplace 
equation using the conformal eta-Ricci-Yamabe soliton when the soliton's potential 
vector field is a gradient type. Additionally, this research relates an ideal 
fluid's spacetime to a Robertson-Walker spacetime and discusses the soliton's 
expansion/contraction condition in the context of a perfect fluid's spacetime.

To study the rotational characteristics of distorted halos, we utilized the angular momentum projection method on wave functions derived from the deformed relativistic Hartree-Bogoliubov theory in continuum. Our self-consistent approach effectively accounts for interactions between single particle bound states and the rotating halo ground states for rotating oxygen and carbon isotopes. Calculations indicate that for rotating isotopes, a distorted halo shape results in a significant increase in rotational energy that is driven by the inertial moment of the extended halo structure. This effect diminishes with increasing angular momentum due to the increasing overlap between rotating single particle states and the non-rotating halo ground state, causing multiple-level excitations.

A common approach in video super-resolution is the recurrent structure, with the BasicVSR method being one of the top-performing frameworks, leveraging bidirectional propagation and reverse alignment to utilize information from the input video. In our research, we upgrade BasicVSR by incorporating second-order grid propagation and a deformable alignment guided by optical flow, enabling the efficient exploitation of spatial and temporal local similarities. Our enhanced model, BasicVSR++, significantly outperforms the original by achieving a lower PSNR and better SSIM score in most cases, while demonstrating the efficiency of a simplified version without second-order propagation. Moreover, we showcase the versatility of our method by applying it to video super-resolution on real video and obtain impressive results.

Due to the tendency for high-energy lepton colliders to radiate forward and resemble weak boson colliders beyond a few TeV, a new perspective is taken that treats weak bosons as fundamental components of these leptons. Within this context of a muon collider, we examine the implications of W and Z radiation and demonstrate that their effects on pair production processes such as VγVγ, VVHH, and VVττ are significantly impacted, with W radiation having a particularly notable influence. To mitigate these complications, the introduction of an energy threshold for pair production processes, specifically at 3 TeV, is proposed, which would require a corresponding increase in luminosity needs for certain processes.

In multi-task reinforcement learning, using shared representations can greatly
benefit a learner when multiple tasks are interrelated. While this benefit can
be realized through the use of a shared policy network, doing so introduces the
challenge of allocating task experience between individual tasks. We frame this as
a particular type of exponential multi-arm bandit problem, where the value of
each arm (task) is estimated through the shared network and is directly affected by
the other arms. We then propose several upper bounds for solving this problem,
including a novel index-based method that can be efficiently applied. The key
insight behind our solutions is the recognition that the estimated advantages,
which reflect the expected benefits of each task, are a reliable indicator of the
optimal exploration-exploitation trade-off. We provide theoretical guarantees,
along with empirical evidence, to illustrate the effectiveness of our methods in
multi-task discrete action spaces, as well as a linear function approximation
scenario. The code for the proposed algorithms is available at https://github.com/alevans/emab.

The paper provides derivations of Li-Yau and Souplet-Zhang type estimates for the equation $u_t=\Delta_p(u)+\lambda u$ in a bounded domain with various boundary conditions, along with estimates for the equation $\Delta_p(u)=\lambda u$ on the whole space. It also examines the uniqueness of solutions to the equation $\Delta_p(u)=\lambda u$ on the whole space.

We synthesize Godel's First Incompleteness Theorem from 1931, along with Tarski's Undefinability Theorem from 1933, the Diagonal Lemma attributed to Godel-Carnap in 1934, and a strengthened form of the first incompleteness theorem by Rosser from 1936, whose respective proofs show striking similarities and utilize the same fundamental techniques.

This paper formulates the three balls theorem for functions u, subject to specific conditions derived from Clifford analysis. In particular, we leverage these conditions to extend Hadamard's three circles theorem to monogenic functions within R^n+1 space.

When the population is not fully known in advance, sampling occurs in sequence, either individually or in batches, which are obtained sequentially. This work presents a novel algorithm that allows for sequential selection of a balanced sample. The algorithm accommodates equal and unequal inclusion probabilities and can also be applied to select spatially balanced samples when sampling is conducted in person, such as in field surveys. Moreover, the algorithm's efficiency is demonstrated through simulation, and its practical usefulness is illustrated with real-life examples.

In robotics, calibrating an eye-in-hand camera using image information is an essential task that has been extensively researched. We investigated using artificial intelligence-based methods for this purpose by leveraging only a single color image, utilizing exclusively real-world data without any self-supervision techniques. Our approach involved training a neural network with a mapping function, which takes an image and a 3D point in the environment and predicts the corresponding pixel value. The network was optimized to estimate its own parameters and those of a pose regression module, which produces a probability distribution representing possible camera orientations. We tested this approach with 300,000 images captured by a moving camera from the SUN3D dataset and evaluated its performance on 10,000 unseen images, also from this dataset. Our results show that this entirely self-supervised artificial intelligence method can accurately determine camera poses, with results comparable to those obtained with methods that add noise to real data during training.

In inverse problems, researchers seek a probability distribution that accurately describes the solution based on noisy data and an incomplete model. This distribution is typically sampled using Markov Chain Monte Carlo methods, but these methods can produce slow mixing chains, leading to inaccurate results. An alternative approach involves training a generative adversarial network within the context of the desired data distribution to bypass the sampling process. However, current GAN training methods often fail to converge and don't account for the invertibility of the underlying map. Our research proposes a new objective function that leverages the uniqueness of the underlying map to create a GAN model. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through image deconvolution tests.

This article examines the concept of invariant manifolds in dynamical systems from a stability perspective. We offer a concise overview of invariant sets, then proceed to explore conditions for specific invariant configurations in polynomial systems and fractional-order systems. Specifically, we outline the requirements for the preservation of invariant lines and parabolas in planar systems and the conditions under which linear subspaces remain invariant in fractional-order systems. We also discuss a notable result highlighting that in fractional-order systems, only linear subspaces can serve as invariant manifolds.

Next-generation wireless networks require exceptionally high data transfer rates that could be achieved by utilizing Terahertz frequency bands for communication. Traditionally, THz communication is confined to short-distance applications because THz signals face high absorption in the atmosphere. To overcome this limitation, researchers have explored the potential of multi-hop directional transmission techniques to extend communication range, albeit these schemes can result in prolonged beam training time using conventional methods such as exhaustive search or hierarchical approaches. To tackle this problem, a novel hierarchical beam training technique is proposed in this paper that dynamically optimizes training levels across individual single-hop links, maximizing overall spectral efficiency. To tackle this optimization problem in the presence of channel state uncertainty and noise, a reinforcement learning solution inspired by the multi-armed bandit problem is proposed. Simulations show the new technique converges quickly in dynamic channel conditions and offers up to 75% better performance than conventional methods in terms of spectral efficiency.

The interstellar medium is home to many scattering screens, most of which have not been fully mapped. A new method is introduced for analyzing screen properties using pulsar scintillation data. This method is grounded in Bayesian statistics and takes into account the stochastic nature of data. It is shown that the standard method of studying screens is a special case of this new approach. The method is tested on data from scintillation observations of the pulsar PSR B1133+16. The results indicate that the method is capable of recovering screen properties with a high degree of accuracy. It is also demonstrated that the new approach can differentiate between multiple-scattering effects and those caused by a single screen.

This paper presents a generative model called Quasi-Periodic WaveNet (QPNet) to enhance the limited pitch control of WaveNet (WN) through pitch-dependent dilated convolution neural networks. WN achieves high-fidelity audio generation using stacked dilated convolution layers as an autoregressive probabilistic model. However, the lack of prior knowledge and the pure data-driven nature of WN lead to pitch control difficulties, particularly in modeling periodic signal components for inputs outside the training frequency range. To overcome this challenge, QPNet is proposed with two innovations. Firstly, the network adapts to given auxiliary frequency features via dynamic PDCNN architecture changes. Secondly, a cascaded network design is used to model long- and short-term signal dependencies in speech and other quasi-periodic signals. Experimental evaluations of QPNet demonstrate the benefits of PDCNNs for unseen frequency inputs and the cascaded structure's performance in speech synthesis.

This research presents a novel annotation and correction tool for Arabic texts,
namely MADARi, catering to Standard and Dialectal varieties. MADARi offers a user-
friendly interface and efficient management capabilities for annotating and handling
a considerable volume of texts. Its key features include a set of pre-defined dialect
categories, a classification system and a set of morphological analyzers. Additionally,
MADARi incorporates a built-in error correction module, inspired by the Guessing
Game framework, allowing it to leverage human judgment in resolving annotation
discrepancies. The tool excels in both annotating and handling Arabic texts, as seen in
our case study reported in the paper.

Planets similar to Earth, orbiting nearby stars with reduced energy output, are being extensively studied and several are found to have conditions suitable for ammonia presence. Research indicates that ammonia could end up in methane cycle interactions, leading to significant toxic by-products. These toxic compounds might also result from methane breakdown in ammonia-rich environments. Our model examines systems where methane and ammonia interact, considering various planetary temperatures and reactive gas depths. It's found that moderate temperatures trigger a substantial methane-to-hydrogen conversion, yielding phosphine and ammonia ice accumulation. Warmer temperatures lead to reduced reactive gas layers, decreasing phosophine production. Cooler temperatures, on the other hand, fail to initiate substantial photochemical reactions. Research indicates that ammonia may contribute to the disappearance of methane, but also highlights how methane contributes to ammonia disappearance. The models indicate that highly reactive systems may limit ammonia and methane availability, while less reactive systems allow both gases to build up, causing significant photochemical toxicity.

To differentiate between zero-energy peaks originating from Majorana and those from other causes at non-zero temperatures, our method involves superconducting critical current measurements in addition to tunneling conductivity analysis. A fluctuation Doppler shift in the former technique provides unambiguous Majorana signatures. Our approach enables unambiguous detection of zero-energy peaks, which disappear at non-zero temperatures, reducing Majorana signatures to unrecognizable remnants. In models with isolated vortices, the Majorana peak's conductivity fades as temperature increases, whereas in model scenarios with paired vortices, the conductivity shows temperature independence, exhibiting no clear Majorana signature in our simulated magnetic fields.

The development of advanced detection algorithms through deep learning has accelerated the development of automated road inspection technologies. To expedite and reduce costs associated with road maintenance, a comprehensive system incorporating a vehicle-mounted platform equipped with a detection system was devised. This system leverages a sophisticated detection algorithm based on a deep learning framework, supported by an optimized database containing over 10,000 images, to identify and prioritize defects. To enhance the system's performance, a optimized strategy was developed to manage data processing, incorporating a hierarchical classification approach. This led to a significant enhancement in classification accuracy and a reduction in processing time. The optimized strategy and associated algorithms were implemented using C++ programming, and system testing was conducted along the 428 km stretch of China's G4 highway, resulting in a 96.5% detection rate for cracks, a 95.6% detection rate for potholes, and a 97.3% detection rate for edge drops.

The theory of shadows constitutes an axiomatic bicategorical framework, independently developed by Shulman in 2017 and by Cockett and Tripathi in 2019. This 2019 study shows that the theory of shadows exactly replicates the axioms of the 2-category of bicategories through a process called self-reference, utilizing a morphism-like approach. Furthermore, after defining a bicategorical version of shadow mapping for 2-arrows in the context of Morita, it is demonstrated that the theory of shadows results from the axioms of 2-categories being cartesian closed, with the natural formation of products, by connecting the theory of shadows to the concept of CCC via the functor category [CCC, CCC].

Our primary goal in this research is to pinpoint sound sources within video frames without relying on manually labeled data. Our core innovation involves training the network to distinguish between difficult image elements, including those that include the object generating the sound, to significantly enhance sound source localization performance. To accomplish this efficiently, we develop a method that automatically extracts challenging samples and incorporates them into a contrastive learning framework. Our algorithm achieves superior results on the Flickr SoundNet dataset, a prominent benchmark. Moreover, we introduce a new dataset called VGG-Sound Source, a comprehensive set of annotated video clips featuring sound sources with explicit bounding box markings. VGG-Sound Source surpasses existing datasets in scale, size, and category diversity, comprising 5,000 videos spanning over 200 categories. Notably, it differs from Flickr SoundNet in that it is based on video data. We hope that VGG-Sound Source will contribute positively to the progress of sound source localization research and encourage network architecture innovation through challenge-winning entries in the Sound Source Localization Leaderboard.

Recent advancements in graph convolutional networks (GCNs) are largely based on Euclidean geometry, but many real-world networks exhibit scale-free or hierarchical patterns that can be efficiently represented within hyperbolic geometry. This leads to improved efficiency and reduced computational cost when applying graph neural networks (GNNs). Our novel HyperGCN framework adapts the graph convolutional layer for non-Euclidean spaces by formulating the hyperbolic graph convolution and multi-layer perception (MLP) components. Furthermore, our approach leverages fixed-point arithmetic for hyperbolic operations while ensuring precise results through the incorporation of a correction layer. Comprehensive experiments across multiple datasets demonstrate enhanced performance compared to standard GCNs, while fixed-point implementations show significant speedup without compromising accuracy.

This research focuses on resolving an inverse problem where a source within an acoustic wave is identified, and we aim to estimate the source's distribution and the structural acoustic system's damping parameter within a partially accessible domain. The acoustic wave is modeled by a partial differential equation, and we have access to incomplete boundary measurements via a flexible boundary, which makes the problem challenging. However, the issue can be framed as an ill-posed problem and tackled using a regularization approach. We explore a Tikhonov regularization method and a Carleman estimate-based method to recover the source and damping parameter. Key aspects, including uniqueness and stability results, are established and demonstrated through numerical experiments using a computational model.

A new method has been created that successfully transfers squeezed states into optical cavities even in stable conditions. The method builds upon conventional optomechanical setups, utilizing a three-level atom to facilitate the transfer. Two techniques were devised to observe the squeezed state transfer effect, including applying a controlled influx of squeezed phonons and simulating the system in an environment of phonon-squeezed vibrations. Our model demonstrates the ability to efficiently achieve this transfer in optomechanical systems.

We examine an expansion of modal $\mu$-calculus, specifically considering its application to sets defined by transitive closure. Our analysis focuses on set interpretations where the partial order is finite and composed of cycle-free components. We explore the complexity of model checking this expanded modal $\mu$-calculus and demonstrate that, for certain structures without cyclic components, the problem is decidable by reducing it to a problem solvable through atomic query evaluation. Conversely, the undecidability of model checking is shown for infinite structures with cyclic components by reduction from the satisfiability problem of the expanded modal $\mu$-calculus. Furthermore, we establish that the addition of a single operator, akin to the 1-operator in traditional $\mu$-calculus, suffices to attain undecidability in infinite contexts.

We present a novel exponential delay discounting model incorporating
phases of impulsivity and self-control, inspired by the dual process theory.
This model integrates the concepts of impulsivity and time preference to offer
a more comprehensive framework for understanding delay discounting, where the
discount rate fluctuates based on the current phase of the individual's mental
state. We utilize a hidden Markovian approach to capture the dynamic nature
of the delay discounting process and estimate model parameters using maximum
likelihood estimation. Our method is applicable to a wide range of exponential
delay discounting models and is particularly useful for analyzing data exhibiting
irregular patterns, such as non-linear time trends or anomalous data points.

When considering linearized gravity within a harmonic gauge theory for a symmetric tensor field, implementing the harmonic gauge yields three independent gauge components rather than the expected five, as the gauge infinitesimally maintains its form. This observation leads to the creation of additional third-order differential operators for each missing component, resulting in a new gauge-invariant operator for each missed component. If the original symmetric tensor is expressed in terms of a traceless part, the additional operators will each act on the original tensor's spatial components, and when this action is combined with the original fifth-order de Donder operator, the resulting operator will be invariant under the entire Poincaré group.

A signed graph is created by adding a polarity to the edges of an existing graph, and this concept of signed graphs has recently been integrated with other graph theory ideas like minors and coloring. By examining the notion of extended double covers, we explore new possibilities for signed graph theory. A specific type of graph, known as a K_4 minor, is of particular interest and has intriguing properties - it can be constructed from a set of 4 vertices by ensuring that no two vertices are connected directly. We then establish a new condition known as beta-kappa-four independence number, and this condition applies specifically to 4-vertex graphs with K_4 minors and can be determined deterministically.

For a class of quadratic Hamiltonians, a transformation of Weyl-Wigner symbols through a change of variables reveals the canonical thermal equilibrium quantum states, using the Weyl-Wigner representations and metaplectic operators, whose associated unitary classical structures behave predictably under the transformation, exposing a diagonalizing Liouvillean matrix that determines the key thermodynamic properties, including temperature, chemical potential, and chemical capacitance, which are found to be non-linear and potentially unstable, leading to unusual hysteresis behavior in the equilibrium energy for certain Hamiltonians.

The notion of negative absolute temperature has been substantiated, and it's now widely accepted as a viable concept in both statistical mechanics and thermodynamics. We'll offer a primer on this idea, explaining why it's not merely a mathematical construct. In doing so, we'll explore the measurement procedures, the associated implications, and offer a statistical framework that acknowledges the possibility of negative temperatures. Specifically, we'll discuss Gibbs distribution, extract relevant information such as temperature, and demonstrate the efficacy of our approach using simulated laser data.

Let G be an abelian group and A a nonempty subset of G, with elements indexed as $a_0, a_1,..., a_{k-1}$. For any positive integer h less than or equal to k, we can calculate a restricted signed sumset denoted as $h\hat{}_{\underline{+}}A$, which comprises sums of $a_i$ with weights from {-1,0,1}. The goal of this article is to investigate the minimum number of elements in $\hat{}_{\underline{+}}A$ when A is a sequence of consecutive integers. We demonstrate that the minimum number of elements in $\hat{}_{\underline{+}}A$ is $a_0+a_1+1$ when A starts from 1. Additionally, we provide evidence that the minimum number of elements in $\hat{}_{\underline{+}}A$ is at least $a_0+a_1+2$ for any set A of consecutive integers, excluding 0, thereby broadening a previous result by the second author.

Characterizing colorectal polyps histopathologically is crucial to personalize patient treatment and follow-up, ultimately reducing the risk of undetected invasive carcinomas. The process of polyp characterization involves examining tissue samples for malignancy and dysplasia using histological analysis. Recent advancements in deep learning have significantly improved medical diagnosis accuracy, but training these models requires vast amounts of clinical data. In this context, we've developed UniNet, a deep learning network that uses a unified, progressive learning approach to analyze colorectal polyps from low-resolution whole-slide images. UniNet employs a progressive learning strategy to handle samples at varying histological grades, leveraging a single unified model rather than separate models for individual grades. Our experiments demonstrated that UniNet surpasses current state-of-the-art techniques and can effectively differentiate between different histological grades, even with limited training data. Furthermore, UniNet received significant performance boosts through the incorporation of additional training datasets. Our innovative unified learning approach offers a promising framework for medical image analysis, allowing for efficient training with a single model.

A novel numerical approach has been introduced for solving time-harmonic acoustic scattering issues, primarily centered around analyzing the impact of smoothly varying material inhomogeneities on plane waves. This method's efficiency is optimal for high-frequency scenarios and is adaptable across any given frequency $\omega$. The approach operates within a time-domain framework, consisting of three main components: generating a suitable incoming plane wave with compact propagation direction, solving the time-domain scattering problem, and ultimately extracting the time-harmonic scattered field via the Fourier transform. Key advantages of this approach include: (1) determination of optimal orientation for plane waves susceptible to tunneling, (2) reduced computational domain volume due to Fourier transform application, and (3) opportunity for domain size minimization in subsequent Fourier transform applications. Several techniques to minimize the computational domain are explored and demonstrated through numerical examples. Furthermore, the method has been implemented in the Dippy software platform developed by the University College London.

We analyzed the isotopic composition of hydrogen and water content in pyroxene minerals from recent chondrite falls in Benenitra (2018) and Chelyabinsk (2013), as well as three older chondrite finds in Antarctica. In contrast to the water-rich Antarctic samples with terrestrial contamination, Benenitra and Chelyabinsk pyroxene minerals showed lower levels of water (around 0.018-0.087 wt.$\%$ H$_2$O) and D-poor isotopic signatures (-69$\leq$\delta$^2$Eu$\leq$-17$\permill$). These findings suggest a more primitive water composition in the chondrites' original solar material, with an average D-puicity 1.5 times lower than reported in the Leachian chondrites. Additionally, the water isotopic data show a correlation with chondrite matrix, suggesting the incorporation of matrix material during the formation of pyroxene. A simple thermal reaccumulation model of the chondrite matrix is unable to account for the observed water and deuterium distribution, indicating the presence of a more complex thermal history or other processes such as the occurrence of highly volatile elements in the chondrites.

Using the algebraic Bethe-ansatz method, we find exact expressions for scalar products and form factors of higher-spin XXZ chains. This applies to any spin values and mixtures thereof. We show that affine quantum-group symmetry plays a key role in deriving the exact expressions, particularly for monodromy matrix elements. As a result, we obtain general expressions that combine multiple spin values. For a single chain with a specific spin value, we obtain specific expressions and confirm previous algebraic- Bethe-ansatz findings. Furthermore, we derive exact expressions for form factors and scalar products for multiple chains.

Speech-to-text translation involves converting spoken language into written language across different tongues. Conventional two-stage approaches using speech recognition and machine translation have inherent flaws, including the amplification of inaccuracies. A single-stage approach offers a more unified and less error-prone alternative. Zero-shot speech-to-text translation presents an innovative challenge, where the speech and text languages do not overlap, requiring the development of new techniques for out-of-vocabulary words. This work delves into a zero-shot speech-to-text translation model using parallel text data for English and German, with the goal of generating text in German from spoken English. The principal difficulty in this task lies in handling unfamiliar words during speech recognition, which are absent from the training speech corpus. To tackle this problem, we leverage the zero-shot learning capability of the text-to-text transformer encoder, specifically T5, by training the decoder to generate the speech spectrum from spoken languages. This decoder, in turn, is trained to decode the speech spectrum and generate German text. Our experimental results on zero-shot speech-to-text translation demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach, surpassing the performance of baseline methods, including direct speech-to-text translation.

We assess the applicability of three different methods for calculating electromagnetic multipoles: Cartesian primitive multipoles, irreducible multipoles and spherical multipoles. Our findings suggest that the spherical multipoles provide the most accurate description of electromagnetic scattering behavior, as demonstrated with an example of an amorphous silicon sphere. These multipoles are utilized to model the optical force exerted on particles composed of semiconductors, dielectrics, and metals over a broad range of wavelengths spanning from the dipolar regime down to the Mie regime.

This study introduces two categories of elements in the algebra U(gl(n)), specifically double Young-Capelli bitableaux and central Schur elements, both displaying remarkable action on the highest weight vectors of irreducible Schur modules. The central Schur elements can be viewed as a sum of double Young-Capelli bitableaux corresponding to various strictly increasing Young tableaux. These elements equate to preimages under the Harish-Chandra isomorphism of shifted Schur polynomials, aligning with quantum immanants as per Okounkov. Notably, the representation of Schur elements/quantum immanants bypasses reliance on irreducible characters of symmetric groups. The central Schur elements/quantum immanants exhibit compatibility with promotion on the lattice of Young tableaux, with some displaying the role of intertwining operators, and others being responsible for shifting the dominant weights.

Within the simplest scoto-seesaw framework, we establish a link between neutrino oscillation lengths and the 'atmospheric' and'solar' mass scales. This relationship arises from the interconnection between the two distinct mass scales mentioned earlier. Consequently, the smallest neutrino mass directly correlates with the smallest of the two mass scales, while the largest oscillation length is tied to the largest of the two, with an additional constant factor. This connection results in a specific range for the smallest neutrino mass, which falls within the detection capabilities of current and upcoming experiments. If the smallest neutrino mass lies above the sensitivity of these experiments, we can still derive a bound for the largest oscillation length, which would be within the observable range for long-baseline neutrino experiments such as DUNE.

We employ exact diagonalization to examine a central hypothesis in transition metal oxides, which is often that $t_{2g}$ and $e_g$ orbital states are isolated from one another due to symmetry. However, in many cases, particularly in correlated systems, $t_{2g}$-$e_g$ mixing can be quite substantial, often amounting to as much as 50%. Our research provides the $d$-shell exact diagonalization data that is missing from the existing literature, which is necessary for understanding the effects of $t_{2g}$-$e_g$ mixing on the spectral properties of superconducting materials like cuprates and nickelates.

This research examines how relative quantum cohomology evolves under certain mathematical transformations known as birational transformations. Specifically, it investigates the properties of relative I-functions in the context of toric complete intersections. For a particular type of toric complete intersections with specified divisor properties, it shows that the relative I-functions can be matched directly. Additionally, it demonstrates that the relative I-functions for another class of toric complete intersections can be connected through analytical means. Furthermore, it explores connections between these results and the related mathematical theories of extremal transitions and FJRW.

Using generative adversarial networks, a novel application in disease detection has emerged, leveraging realistic synthetic data. However, GANs were primarily tested with limited datasets. Our research utilizes a StyleGAN version 2 to create realistic X-rays across a broad spectrum, spanning 14 different conditions, as depicted in the OID dataset. By manipulating attributes and performing cross-domain transfers, we successfully developed a technique for creating synthetic X-rays by inputting text descriptions. Our method was further tested on an outer chest dataset, yielding promising results. Experimentation revealed how GAN learned to identify and separate outer and inner chest images. In addition, a synthetic dataset was used to train a convolutional neural network for lung nodule detection, producing comparable performance to models trained on actual data.

ViDaExpert is an application for multidimensional data visualization and
advanced analysis. It is capable of handling object-feature tables that include
numerical values and text-based labels for objects and features. The tool
encompasses several statistical techniques such as weighted PCA, elastic maps,
linear discriminant analysis, and decision tree construction, in addition to
K-Means clustering and multilinear regression. With customizable visualizations
and an interactive 3D viewer, ViDaExpert supports the creation of 3D scenes
from data and enables drag-and-drop loading of Kobe objects for external use
in presentations and educational contexts.

Evaluating Newtonian potentials over complex two-dimensional regions efficiently is crucial for solving Poisson's equation and volume integral equations numerically. For domains with irregular boundaries, using a grid without a set pattern necessitates an unstructured approach. We present an unstructured algorithm for a fast evaluation of Newtonian potentials based on a novel application of Green's identity, which overcomes difficulties associated with unstructured grids. The method overcomes challenges posed by unstructured grids and provides a significant improvement in computational efficiency. The method has been implemented and its performance is compared with a straightforward approach using interpolated values of the potential on a grid with a set pattern. The comparison shows that the new algorithm achieves a substantial improvement in computational speed, particularly for large domains and tight grid sizes.
